description: Issue summary: Customer reports that while viewing a dashboard with tenant-scoped filters applied, switching organizations via the org selector clears filter state and causes tracing hook links to open in the newly-selected org context. Impact: Customer-facing dashboards show metrics for the wrong organization after org-switch during the same browser session; trace links in alert emails and dashboard panels resolve to traces in the alternate org resulting in confusion and potential data exposure. Environment: Production, us-east cluster, console frontend v2.11.0, auth service v1.9.2. Observed start: 2026-03-10 10:24 UTC (first customer report).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Log in as a user with access to multiple organizations (tested with an account on QuantaHR orgs: quantahr-prod and quantahr-staging).
2) Open a dashboard under quantahr-prod and apply a tenant-level filter (user=analytics-team, env=prod).
3) Click on a trace-hyperlink in a panel or select 'Open trace' on a span to verify trace context points to quantahr-prod traces (works as expected).
4) Use the top-left org selector to switch to quantahr-staging without refreshing the page.

5) Observe that the applied filters are cleared from the dashboard and any trace links now resolve to quantahr-staging traces; some alert links in the console still surface metrics rows from quantahr-prod but links point to staging tracing - inconsistent behavior.
expected_behavior: Filters and query scope should persist for the active dashboard session unless explicitly cleared by the user or the dashboard is reloaded.

Switching organizations should perform a hard context refresh or clearly indicate that view-scoped filters will be reset; trace links should maintain the original org context for the active page or prompt to confirm context switch before following links.
observed_behavior: Dashboard filters appear to be silently reset when org is switched in the global selector without page reload.
Trace links embedded in panels and alert emails are resolving to the newly-selected org's trace index even though the panel metrics still visually show values from the previous org until a refresh.
logs: frontend console (user session): Uncaught (in promise) Error: failed to hydrate org-context: token mismatch 2026-03-10T10:24:11Z sessionId=abc123
api gateway (request): POST /v2/dashboards/query 2026-03-10T10:24:12Z trace_id=01f2e4ae response=200 org=quantahr-prod user=anna@quantahr.com
api gateway (after switch): POST /v2/traces/lookup 2026-03-10T10:24:13Z trace_id=01f2e4ae response=200 org=quantahr-staging user=anna@quantahr.com
auth service: issued_token org_claim=quantahr-staging for session abc123 at 2026-03-10T10:24:12.500Z
investigation_notes: Support replicated issue with a multi-org test account. Behavior reproducible when org switch is done via client-side selector without a full page reload.

Hypothesis 1: frontend state store merges new org claim into session context without invalidating per-view filter state leading to mismatch between filter UI and subsequent API calls that carry new org header.

Hypothesis 2: trace link generation uses a separate codepath that reads current session org claim from the auth token at click time rather than preserving the org scoped to the originating panel result set.

Checked console trace: token refresh is occurring immediately after org switch (auth service issued new token) but dashboard panels remain rendered with values fetched under previous token until next query.
impact: QuantaHR has reported confusion among analytics and security teams; two alerts were escalated to on-call because links did not match displayed metrics.
Risk: potential data cross-view confusion and temporary exposure of links to orgs that the user still has access to but did not intend to view.
workaround: Advise user to refresh the browser after switching organizations to ensure UI and API context are consistent (documented as temporary guidance to QuantaHR Support contact).
If needing to keep the original organization's context while inspecting a dashboard, open the dashboard in an incognito window or separate browser profile before switching orgs in the main session.
resolution_notes: Engineering action items: (1) modify frontend org-switch flow to perform a deterministic full-context refresh or explicitly clear per-view filter state when org changes, (2) update trace link generation to attach originating-org metadata at render time so links remain consistent even if session token changes later in the session.
PR created to enforce refresh-on-org-switch: github.com/redwood/console/pull/7632 (adds opt-in config to preserve previous behavior for low-latency environments).

Targeted patch schedule: bugfix branch v2.11.1 to be cut 2026-03-13; patch will be deployed to staging for validation and then rolled to prod in a canary group of 5% of console hosts before global rollout.
Post-deploy validation: run automated UI flow that switches orgs and clicks trace links to assert origin org header remains attached to generated trace links.
follow_up_tasks: Add e2e test to CI for org-switch + dashboard filter persistence (assigned to eng: frontend-team).
Update user-facing docs/FAQ to explain behavior until fix is live (assigned to docs).
Create a postmortem if similar incidents occur with P0 customer impact (support lead to monitor for 72 hours post-rollout).
comments: Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-10: Customer reported that dashboards displayed metrics from quantahr-prod but trace links opened quantahr-staging traces after switching orgs mid-session. Requested root cause and ETA for fix.

Customer (Anna Martinez, QuantaHR) 2026-03-10: Confirmed steps and provided a short screencast. Says this caused an on-call pager noise due to mismatched links. Asking for a short-term mitigation aside from hard refresh.

SRE (Luca Bianchi) 2026-03-11: Captured gateway logs showing token re-issuance on org switch. Suggest ensuring any client-side cached org-scoped request headers are invalidated immediately after org claim change.
Frontend Eng (Elena Park) 2026-03-11: Drafted PR to force reload-on-org-switch and to include 'originatingOrg' metadata on panel results. Assigning validation to QA.
